title: Reduce Terraform plan noise with lifecycle hooks and staged apply
creator: Aisha Khan
description:
Background: Over the last 12 months we've seen an uptick in spurious terraform plan diffs across networking and shared modules caused by provider upgrades, auto-generated tags, and lifecycle-sensitive resources (EIP recreation, NAT attachment churn). These noisy plans increase CI churn, slow merges, and drive rollbacks when engineers misinterpret plan output.

Goal: Reduce plan noise and plan-time surprises for infra teams by introducing a combination of lifecycle.ignore_changes conventions, explicit lifecycle hooks for high-risk resources, and a staged-apply workflow in CI. This work should reduce the median number of false-positive diffs in the networking module by >70% and cut plan-related pipeline reruns by 50%.

Proposed approach:
1) Module-level convention: establish a consistent lifecycle.ignore_changes whitelist for computed tags and DNS-ownership fields. Document the convention in the module README and add a linter rule to our tfsec/terrafmt pipeline.
2) Introduce a lightweight lifecycle-hook module (null_resource-based with triggers) that standardizes pre-create checks (eg. availability of EIPs, orphaned route tables) and a post-apply reconciliation step to reconcile provider-level drift that we deliberately ignore during plan.
3) Staged apply: Add a pipeline stage that runs terraform plan for all workspaces but gates apply for networking-critical modules behind a manual or canary approval. For PRs touching these modules we will run an automated 'staged-apply -dryrun' job which simulates resource creation order and reports likely replacements.
4) Provider pin and provider-init improvements: pin major provider versions in module root and decouple provider upgrade from resource changes using provider_install.sh to mitigate provider-init causing diffs. Ensure terraform-provider-lock.json is committed for shared modules.
5) Nightly drift detection & cleanup: expand our nightly drift job to produce a tidy list of ignored diffs and recommend changes to ignore list, reducing long-term signal loss.

Out of scope: full module rewrite or large API design changes. This PR is focused on conventions and tooling so we can get quick wins and reduce CI flakiness.

Acceptance criteria:
- New lifecycle conventions documented and adopted by >=3 core infra modules.
- CI linter enforces missing lifecycle.ignore_changes for configured computed attributes.
- Staged-apply pipeline is added and used for at least all networking workspaces.
- Measurable reduction in plan churn (target >=70% fewer false positives on sample runs).

Risks & trade-offs:
- Overuse of ignore_changes hides real issues. To mitigate, we will scope ignore lists narrowly and run nightly drift detection.
- Manual gated applies increase friction; mitigated by enabling canary allows and a short TTL for automatic gate lift once CI confidence is high.

Rollout plan:
Phase 1 (this ticket): add conventions, lifecycle-hook module, CI linter rule, provider lock guidance, and one pilot module (shared-networking).
Phase 2: extend to other modules, tune nightly drift, and add dashboard for ignored diffs.
Phase 3: review after 30 days, loosen manual gating if metrics stable.

Estimated effort: 5 points across 2 engineers over 2 sprints.
